state.name: clock

why: Clock mode and pending waits are private driver bookkeeping owned by a resource, as ADR 0100 requires. Supplier and payment state remain in data cells.

state.name: middleware

why: The factory is synchronous. Its HTTP callbacks own completion of a request. The stop signal gates log writes, delayed rules, and unfinished uploads; a graceful close must still send completed replies.

state.name: listener

why: The pending-response set is private socket bookkeeping used to drain the listener. It is not watched domain state and cannot be a plain serializable data cell.

state.name: listener

why: After listening, the factory registers cleanup and reads the TCP address; it starts no new work. Cleanup drains owned replies, then closes sockets. Fetch callbacks cancel unfinished bodies on the shared stop signal.

state.name: finishDelivery

why: Running delivery delegates to sendWebhook. Its client fetch observes both the service stop signal and the operation signal. There is no defer-only stop in this operation.

state.name: webhooks

why: Defer removes the watcher. Each running child is a deliver operation that observes service stop and ctx.signal, then uses the abortable webhook client.

state.name: inFlight

why: Pending promises and resolvers are private request bookkeeping owned by this resource. Only settled payment keys and domain state live in data.

state.name: inFlight

why: The map starts no running work. Middleware owns each request and resolves/deletes its pending key in finally, including the handler-throw path. Defer only clears the owned registry.
